newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Settlers plan campaign against Israeli government.
newsitem.headline: Settlers plan campaign against Israeli government.

text.p: Jewish settlers pledged to demonstrate on Friday against an Israeli troop redeployment from the West Bank town of Hebron which is being finalised by Israeli and Palestinian negotiators.
"We are starting a battle against the government." said Pinhas Wallerstein, chairman of the umbrella council of the 130,000 Jewish settlers of the West Bank and Gaza.
"We will demonstrate on Friday morning against the government's policy on Hebron while the government is holding its weekly meeting," Wallerstein said.

Palestinian and Israeli negotiators continued to struggle into Friday morning to clinch a deal that would clear the way for Israel to transfer most of Hebron to Palestinian rule. Some 400 Jews live in the heart of the city of about 100,000 Arabs.

Israel has completed many of the security arrangements to transfer 80 percent of the town, a flashpoint of violence, to Palestinian rule. But Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu wants to modify the Hebron accord signed by his Labour Party predecessor last year to bolster safeguards for the settlers.

U.S. State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said on Thursday that special Middle East envoy Dennis Ross believed the sides would need more than two days to reach accord. A senior U.S. official said: "We think they probably have a week to go."

In Cairo, a Middle East economic conference of about 2,500 delegates from 92 countries ended on Thursday with the message that prosperity in the region was within grasp if only the peace talks between Israel and its Arab neighbours could be advanced.
"If you lose peace, everyone will be the loser. If we put the peace process back on track, everyone will gain," Egyptian Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri told the closing session.

In the Hebron talks, Israeli and Palestinian officials said the two sides were deadlocked over Israel's demand that its forces be allowed to enter PLO-run parts of the town when it deems it necessary.
The original agreement permits Israeli forces to enter Hebron only when in "hot pursuit" of suspected attackers.
The Palestinians are also pushing for a written Israeli commitment to carry out further redeployments in West Bank rural areas promised by the previous government.
Israeli media said Netanyahu wanted a reciprocal Palestinian commitment to peace deals and a promise to fight "terrorism".
"We fought for Netanyahu to become prime minister and look what has happened," Wallerstein said.
"I hope this fight we have started will force him to listen to those who voted for him and are now forced to fight against him," he said.
Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai ordered the transfer of additional force to Hebron to prevent unrest over the weekend, Israeli media said.
Jewish settlers have warned of bloodshed should a pullback be implemented.
Hebron's Palestinians have a similiar fear. U.S.-born Baruch Goldstein, a Jew from the adjacent Kiryat Arba settlement, massacred 29 Palestinians in Hebron in 1994.
